the GMI effect in Co-rich microwire is strongly affected by the magnetoelastic anistropy.
the GMI effect in the microwires is a result of the magnetoelastic anistropy and that the low field hysteresis in GMI curves can be suppressed by the bias currents.

the magnetoelastic anistropy is responsible for low field GMI hystersis, which can be suppressed by the bias field.

the microwires have a great potential for applications as GMI sensor.
the GMI effect can be controlled by the bias current and magnetoelastic anistropy.
we have shown that GMI in microwire is a promising candidate for magnetic sensors and magnetic field sensors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microwires with high magnetoelastic anistropy and low saturation field are promising candidates for magnetic field sensors based on GMI.
microwires with low magnetoelastic anistropy and low coercivity are suitable for GMI sensors.
